newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PALM OIL - Laurics - S.E. Asian prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: PALM OIL - Laurics - S.E. Asian prices seen mixed.

text.p: Southeast Asian palm oil prices are expected to be mixed this week with the Malaysian market seen staying firm on the back of strong export demand, regional traders said.
Palm oil prices in Indonesia are likely to remain weak while Philippine coconut oil prices are expected to move sideways to slightly lower, they said.
Traders said Malaysian palm oil prices, trading at three-month highs, may see some consolidation, but strong exports for August should keep the market firm through the week.

"The market appears to be overbought but there's still a lot of buying interest," said one trader. "And if the August export numbers are very good, as speculated, I don't see a market reversal just yet."
Talk circulated in the market on Friday that cargo surveyor Caleb Brett will come out with an export estimate of a record 678,000 tonnes for August.
August export estimates from Caleb Brett and another cargo surveyor, Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS), are due for release on Monday.
Exports in July were 646,017 tonnes, the second highest monthly figure ever recorded. The all-time high was 658,200 tonnes exported in January 1994.
Traders said a recent pick-up in export business has helped dispel earlier concerns that domestic palm oil stocks would reach one million tonnes this year.
They said export demand, particularly from India, would continue to support prices in the near-term.
Traders said exports to India, a major market in recent months, are expected to remain strong in coming months.
Industry officials in India have said the country might import up to 250,000 tonnes of palm olein during the Hindu festival months of September and October to offset thin domestic supplies.
Most of the oil is likely to come from Malaysia as Indonesia, another leading exporter, is facing tight domestic supply, Malaysian traders said.
On Tuesday, India's State Trading Corporation bought 12,000 tonnes of Malaysian palm olein for September/October shipment.
Benchmark third position crude palm oil futures closed on Friday at 1,238 ringgit a tonne, up from 1,196 a week earlier.
Indonesian palm olein prices are expected to remain low as buyers held back on rumours of government plans to import cooking oil from Malaysia.

"I think prices will tend to remain low in the coming week as the market is still filled with uncertainties. Buyers are afraid to buy following rumours of cooking oil import from Malaysia," one trader said.
Indonesia's state logistics agency BULOG has said it planned to intervene in the market and push palm olein prices down in an effort to stabilise cooking oil prices.
Traders said palm olein in Jakarta eased to between 1,490 rupiah/kg and 1,500 rupiah/kg last week from 1,525 rupiah/kg and 1,550 rupiah/kg.
Philippine traders said a rising supply of coconut oil would continue to pressure prices this week.
"I expect prices to move in a narrow $15 range in the coming week," said one Manila trader.
Traders said the coconut oil price for September shipment was last quoted at $685 FOB per tonne on Thursday from $725 at the start of the week.
(With contributions from Jakarta/Manila)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603 230 8911)
